title: Orders with customer names
prompt: The packing team wants each order with the name and city of the customer who placed it. Write `solve(orders, customers)` so it returns `order_id`, `name`, `city` and `total`.
rules: Match an order to the customer with the same `customer_id`.
Leave out orders whose customer isn't in `customers`, and don't list customers who have no orders.
Return only `order_id`, `name`, `city` and `total`, in that order. Keep duplicate orders.
hints: Both tables have a `customer_id` column: pass it as `on=`.
Only rows that match on both sides should stay. Which join type does that?
Join first, then `select` the four columns.
